summary: Drone traffic controllers oversee low-altitude airspace where many uncrewed aircraft fly beyond visual line of sight. Today's closest versions are UTM/U-space service providers, delivery operators' flight-ops centers and the FAA's Dallas UTM key site. Mostly automated systems separate the aircraft (ASTM F3548 strategic deconfliction, Remote ID, LAANC), and the human handles exceptions, coordinates with ATC and public safety, and does compliance work. AI helps most with triaging conflicts and off-nominal events, writing incident and compliance reports, analyzing traffic data, and explaining the fast-changing BVLOS and U-space rules.

prompts.title: Off-nominal event triage
prompts.task: Rank simultaneous conformance alerts and contingencies during a busy shift
prompts.prompt: You are assisting a drone traffic supervisor at a UTM / U-space service provider. Below is a snapshot of active alerts: [PASTE ALERTS: operation IDs, alert type such as non-conforming / contingent / lost C2 link / Remote ID dropout, position, altitude AGL, battery %, nearby operations, airspace class, distance to airports or TFRs]. Rank the alerts by urgency in a table with these columns: rank, operation, hazard, likely cause, suggested next action (contact operator, notify ATC or the airport, broadcast constraint, monitor), and time sensitivity. Then list any alerts that may be linked, for example several drones losing link in the same area. Use only the data given, label your guesses as guesses, and keep it short enough to read in 60 seconds.
prompts.caution: This is decision support only. The certified UTM system and the human supervisor make the calls, and any manned-aircraft or ATC issue follows official procedures.

prompts.title: Operational intent conflict analysis
prompts.task: Review why strategic deconfliction rejected or flagged overlapping flight plans
prompts.prompt: You understand ASTM F3548-21 UTM USS interoperability: operational intents, 4D volumes, priority levels and conformance monitoring. Here are two or more operational intents the deconfliction service flagged: [PASTE VOLUMES: polygons or altitude bands, time windows, priority, states such as Accepted / Activated / Nonconforming, the USS each one came from]. Explain in plain language exactly where and when the volumes intersect. Say whether the rejection or flag looks correct under the standard. Then give 3 ways to resolve it, such as a time shift, an altitude change or a reroute, and estimate the delay each one adds. If the standard is unclear or the data is incomplete, say what you would check in the DSS logs.
prompts.caution: Check your interpretation against the standard text and your USS's own implementation. ASTM standards are copyrighted, so don't paste large excerpts.

prompts.title: Incident report draft
prompts.task: Turn shift logs into a structured incident report and timeline
prompts.prompt: Draft an incident report for a drone event in our managed airspace. Inputs: [PASTE: shift log entries, telemetry summary, Remote ID data, operator statements, ATC communications, weather/METAR]. Use these sections: Summary; Timeline (UTC, one line per event); Aircraft and operator details; Airspace and conditions; What happened; Contributing factors (use a human-factors frame such as HFACS); Immediate actions taken; Open questions; Recommended corrective actions. Keep facts separate from analysis, and mark each statement as [FACT – source] or [ASSESSMENT]. Add a note on whether the event might meet external reporting thresholds, such as FAA Part 107.9 accident reporting or NTSB 49 CFR 830 in the US, or EU 376/2014 occurrence reporting. Frame that note as something for our compliance lead to confirm, not as a conclusion.
prompts.caution: Remove names and personal data before pasting. A qualified person decides whether the event must be reported to regulators.

prompts.title: BVLOS rule change briefing
prompts.task: Learn how proposed or new BVLOS and UTM rules change daily operations
prompts.prompt: I am a drone traffic controller at [ORGANIZATION / COUNTRY]. Brief me on [RULE OR PROPOSAL, e.g. FAA Part 108 BVLOS NPRM and the associated Part 146 automated data service provider rules / EU U-space Regulation 2021/664 / UK CAA BVLOS policy]. Organize the briefing as: (1) what it requires or proposes, in 10 bullets; (2) what changes for traffic management, separation, data services and operator obligations; (3) what is final and what is still proposed, under comment or expected; (4) 5 questions I should ask our compliance team. Your knowledge may be out of date, so mark any detail that could have changed and tell me which official source to check, such as the Federal Register, EASA or the CAA.
prompts.caution: Confirm every point against the current official text. The rules are still changing quickly.

prompts.title: Weekly traffic and safety metrics
prompts.task: Analyze operations data to find trends, hotspots and safety signals
prompts.prompt: You are a safety analyst for a low-altitude traffic service. Here is [PERIOD] of data as CSV: [PASTE OR DESCRIBE COLUMNS: operation ID, operator, start/end time, area, planned vs flown volume, conformance alerts, contingencies, loss-of-link events, near-miss reports, weather]. Calculate total operations, the non-conformance rate per 1,000 flights, the rate of each contingency type, and the busiest time-and-area cells. Flag operators or areas whose numbers are above the norm, using a simple statistical threshold and saying which one you used. Then give 3 hypotheses worth checking and the extra data each would need. Write it as a one-page summary for the operations manager, plus a short appendix explaining your method. Don't infer causes the data can't support.
prompts.caution: A high rate can be a statistical artifact when the number of flights is small, so don't present every flag as a safety finding.

prompts.title: Community and public-safety notice
prompts.task: Explain a new drone corridor or temporary restriction to residents and first responders
prompts.prompt: Write two short communications about [EVENT: e.g. a new delivery drone corridor over [NEIGHBORHOOD] / a temporary flight restriction for [EVENT] / an emergency drone-free zone for wildfire response]. Version A is for residents, under 200 words, at an 8th-grade reading level. It should cover what is happening, when, why it is safe, how to report concerns, and that they can look up drones using Remote ID apps. Version B is for police and fire dispatch. It should cover affected airspace (coordinates, altitude), hours, a 24/7 contact for the drone traffic desk, how to request that drones be cleared from an emergency scene, and how the drones are identified. Details: [PASTE]. Don't overstate safety or make promises we haven't confirmed.
prompts.caution: Have a lawyer or the comms team check privacy statements and liability language before publishing.

prompts.title: Contingency procedure stress-test
prompts.task: Review a lost-link or airspace-clearing procedure for gaps
prompts.prompt: Act as an aviation safety reviewer who uses SORA (JARUS Specific Operations Risk Assessment) style thinking. Review our procedure for [SCENARIO: e.g. lost command-and-control link over a populated area / a manned medevac helicopter entering the UTM area at low altitude / a GNSS outage across the service area / a USS outage]. Procedure text: [PASTE]. Find missing steps, unclear roles, timing that can't work, single points of failure and communication gaps. For each problem, give its severity, a concrete fix and a tabletop exercise question that would test it. Finish with a short checklist version of the improved procedure.
prompts.caution: Treat this review as input to your formal safety management process. Changes still need approval from accountable personnel and, where required, the regulator.

prompts.title: Controller upskilling plan
prompts.task: Build a 12-week learning plan to move from manned ATC or drone piloting into UTM operations
prompts.prompt: I currently work as [BACKGROUND: e.g. tower controller / Part 107 pilot / dispatcher] and want to become a UTM/U-space traffic supervisor in about 12 weeks with [HOURS] hours per week. Build a week-by-week plan covering: UTM concepts (FAA UTM ConOps, NASA UTM research, the FAA Dallas key site), U-space services, ASTM F3548 and Remote ID (F3411 / 14 CFR Part 89), LAANC, detect-and-avoid basics, SORA risk assessment, human factors for supervising automation, and practice data skills. Include free official resources where you know they exist and one practical exercise per week. Flag any resource or credential you are unsure is current, and say which skills employers actually hire for and which are still speculative.
prompts.caution: Check every link and credential yourself, because programs and standards change. No formal drone traffic controller license exists yet in most places.
